content.thinking:
I'm planning the elephant model's proportions and skeleton structure, sizing it like an adult bush elephant facing forward, and starting to lay out the spine chain and hip joint positions carefully to avoid scripting errors.

Now I'm defining the specific coordinates for the spine, tail, and neck chains, deciding on joint counts and parent relationships to build a catmull-rom curve for each body segment.

For the head, I'm shaping the elephant's skull with a high domed forehead, sizing it around 0.9 wide and 1.0 tall, and positioning its center roughly at [0,2.35,2.3] to connect naturally to the neck.

Next I plan the loft stations for the head shape, keeping the geometry low-poly with 8-sided faceted sections rather than smooth ones for a stylized look. Then I'll move on to the trunk, chaining joints from the front of the head down toward the ground with a curling path, treating it as a tentacle-type appendage.

Still defining trunk geometry...

For the tusks, I'm curving them forward-down-out then up using a four-point catmull spline, tapering from a thick ivory-colored root to a sharp tip. The ears come next, modeled as large flat planes rooted at the sides of the head, built from an extruded outline to capture their broad, floppy shape.

Shaping the ear outline to look Africa-like with a flat top, then wrestling with how to splay it outward from the head without skewing the extrusion -- considering a joint pose rotation on the ear hinge instead.

Working out the rotation math: rotating about the Y axis through the ear's joint pivot so the back edge swings outward while the front stays anchored, computing that the sign of the rotation angle needs to flip between the left and right ear so both splay away from the head symmetrically.

Setting up the ear joint with its parent and position, noting the hinge direction probably doesn't matter much since the pose uses model-space axes, and that posing should happen after the ear geometry is extruded. I'm thinking through ear thickness and bevel values, then planning to paint the inner surface with a pinkish gradient or vein pattern rather than building a separate smaller extrude for the inner face.

Blending skin tone and ear-pink using a smooth distance-based mix, adding faint vein lines via a sine-based threshold for subtle shading, then moving on to defining the four legs starting with the front shoulder joint position.

Working out leg proportions: setting the hip joint around body height and the foot target near ground level, with upper and lower leg segment lengths adjusted so the columnar legs reach the floor realistically for an elephant-like stance.

I'm defining the limb chains for front and hind legs, using small bend hints so the legs aren't perfectly straight—slight forward bend at the knee/elbow joints to give a natural stance, with joint names mapped to shoulder/elbow/wrist for front limbs and hip/knee/ankle for hind limbs.

Now setting up the leg sweep radii, tapering from a wider thigh down through the knee to a narrower ankle before reaching the foot.

For the skin texture I'm layering a mottled base color with horizontal wrinkle stripes along the leg, using noise-based wobble so the wrinkle bands look organic rather than mechanically uniform.

Now I'm adding a dusty gradient to the lower legs and body to simulate dirt and weathering, blending from the mottled skin tone into a dustier hue near the ground, then shaping low-poly foot cylinders at the ankle base for the feet.

Still writing foot and toenail geometry...

I'm shifting to the torso now, planning to loft the body shape along the spine path using the spine bone chain to drive deformation.

Defining loft stations for the rump and belly...

I'll skip adding a separate root joint and let the first spine joint own the span before it. Checking the head-to-body connection: the head loft starts near the neck with a slightly smaller width than the body's top radius, so they should overlap cleanly with the rounded cap.

For the head shape itself, I'm defining three loft stations that narrow toward the forehead, plus two small sphere bumps near the top for a dome-like forehead detail. Then I'm setting up the head joint and a simple single-span neck chain connecting the top of the spine to the base of the head.

Now I'm adding the jaw as a small frustum box below the head joint, with a jaw joint oriented downward, and roughing out the trunk root position at the mouth area along with tusk base placements on either side. I'm also starting to position the eyes slightly up and out from the face center.

For the eyes themselves, I'll use the head loft surface to snap spheres onto the actual skin geometry via nearest-point lookup, embedding a dark eyelid sphere and a smaller amber eye sphere into the surface for a natural protruding look.

Now I'm adding paint coats for head wrinkles and toenail color, then building the tail: a tapered sweep along the tail chain plus a tuft of fanned bristle spikes radiating from the tip point for texture at the end.

I'm also adding sparse hair details — a scattered ring of small dark spikes on the forehead area, filtered to only land on the upper head surface for a natural sparse-hair look.

Now I'm thinking about wrinkle details at the knees and elbows, planning to sweep small loop bands around the leg surfaces at a few heights to suggest skin folds.

Using the frame's tangent as default direction for the sweep, I'll build wrinkle rings at each leg joint—four legs with four rings apiece, trusting the sweep loops to resolve even with some risk of failure on tricky bends. I'm also planning dusty tinting on the lower legs and belly, and considering whether to add shoulder/hip bulges for extra body detail.

Working through the leg geometry now: placing hip and shoulder joints with slight offsets so the legs attach smoothly into the body without poking through, checking that limb target distances roughly match the sum of segment lengths for a natural slight bend, and verifying the foot cylinders sit flush with the ground plane.

I'm figuring out joint naming by side (L/R based on sign convention) and parenting the leg chains to the correct spine or pelvis joints, then settling on the color palette — grey-brown skin, darker wrinkle tones, dusty accents, pink ears, and ivory nails.

Now I'm defining the coat shader as a gradient over a mottled, striped pattern blending skin tones with wrinkle color, then fading into a dust tone from the belly down through the legs, keeping the upper body cleaner while the lower limbs pick up more dust.

For the trunk I'm sketching a paint function that creates ring-like banding by checking periodic position along the trunk's length, alternating between the base coat and a darker wrinkle mix to simulate segmented folds.

For the trunk's tip, I'm shaping two small finger-like spikes to mimic an elephant's trunk lips—an upper and lower cone branching off the final joint with slightly different directions—and considering how to render the nostril opening at the very end of the sweep.

Now I'm defining the trunk's sweep chain, tapering radius through successive joints, then moving to head details like cheek bumps and tusk sockets, where I'm placing small skin-colored rings at the tusk bases and plotting the curved tusk path outward and upward from each side of the face.

Shaping the tusks with a tapering radius profile and flat-to-point caps, giving them an ivory gradient from base to tip, then deciding to skip extra ring details and briefly considering spine ridge bumps along the back before moving on.

Now I'm adding belly wrinkle rings by looping around the body surface at a few points along the spine chain, giving slight lifts and thin radii for subtle girth marks, picking four positions spaced along the body's path. I'm also noting I'll skip extra belly sag details and move toward using surface hits for placing the eyes on the head.

For the eyes, I'm computing position with a sign-based offset for left/right, finding the nearest surface point near the target coordinates, and nesting an eyelid sphere and smaller eye sphere embedded into that frame with slight vertical offset. Then I'm setting up the ear joint position and outline orientation, keeping the thickness direction consistent along +X regardless of side so the outline isn't mirrored.

I'm checking that the ear's base position at x=0.46 doesn't collide with the body's shoulder width, and adjusting the rotation angle to 30 degrees so the ear tip swings clear of the torso when posed outward.

I'm sketching the ear outline points to form a convex, bush-ear shape—wide at top, tapering to a rounded hanging tip—using smoothing without sharp corners to keep the silhouette natural.

For coloring, I'm defining a paint function for the ear that blends skin tone with pink interior shading via smoothstep and adds thin vein lines using a sine-based pattern, making sure to return a consistent string/Rgb type so it mixes properly with the skin base color.

Now I'm setting up the ear extrusion parameters (position at earJoint, thickness, bevel, bone attachment), then applying the tilt pose after extrusion since poses should happen after the mesh is built, and noting that hair scatter on the head happens post-pose. Next I want to add toe details and a subtle spine ridge bump to the body.

For the code itself, I'm checking which imports are actually used (THREE, builder, rng, catmull path, limb IK, paint utilities for gradient/mottle effects) to avoid unused import errors, handling the leg tip fallback to the last joint if null, and confirming chains can accept a point array directly. I'm starting the actual builder script now, defining the elephant's pelvis joint as the root spine joint at its position.

Now I'm sketching the spine chain from pelvis forward using a catmull-rom path with three named segments, then lofting the body around that spine with flat-shaded low-poly facets. I'm also defining the tail chain branching off the pelvis with its own catmull path and tapering sweep radius, sharing the same coat color as the body.

Checking that the tail root sits inside the body's rump volume so there's no visible gap, then moving to the neck and head structures: the head gets its own loft, and the trunk sprouts as a chain parented to the head joint with a five-segment catmull path, swept with a tapering radius array for the trunk shape and wrinkle rings.

Now I'm setting up the jaw joint and its frustum-shaped geometry attached to the head, picking a darker skin tone for it while skipping the inner mouth and chin hair details for now. Then I'm writing a loop to generate both front and rear legs symmetrically for left and right sides, defining hip points and limb bend directions, though I'm double-checking how the bend parameter format should be structured for a single direction versus a list.

I'm naming the leg joint chain (shoulder, elbow, wrist per side), setting the parent to the appropriate spine joint, and sweeping a tapered tube along that chain with varying radii to form the leg shape in the coat color. For the feet, I'm placing tapered cylinders at the correct foot positions with flat shading, considering whether to use skin or coat color and how UV painting would map onto the cylinder geometry.

Adding toenails now...

Adjusting the shoulder sphere scale smaller to avoid an odd bulge. For the hind leg, I'm placing the hip near z -1.4 with the knee bending forward toward the target. Now moving on to the tail tuft spikes.

Writing spike generator loop...
